Yorkshire Dales: Scenic Motorcycle Roads

The Yorkshire Dales are a landscape of contrasts — deep limestone valleys with green meadows, exposed hilltop plateaus of peat and heather, and dramatic scars and crags created by geology millions of years ago. The riding roads exploit these contrasts beautifully, climbing from sheltered valley floors to exposed hilltops and back again.

Classic Dales Roads

  • Buttertubs Pass: A high moorland road between Hawes and Thwaite. The pass takes its name from deep limestone potholes beside the road — natural curiosities worth stopping for. The views across Swaledale from the summit are magnificent.
  • Fleet Moss: The highest road in the Dales at 589m, connecting Hawes to Buckden. The gradient is steep (1 in 4 in places) and the surface can be rough, but the exposed moorland setting is dramatic.
  • The B6270 Swaledale Road: Following the River Swale from Richmond to Keld through England's wildest dale. Stone barns, meadows, and waterfalls line the route.
  • Ribblesdale: The B6255 from Settle to Hawes passes the Ribblehead Viaduct — one of England's great engineering landmarks. Time your visit to see a train crossing the arches.

The Dales Valleys

  • Wharfedale: The B6160 through Wharfedale passes through Bolton Abbey (romantic ruins in a river setting) and continues through Grassington and Kilnsey Crag — a dramatic overhanging limestone cliff.
  • Dentdale: A hidden valley in the western Dales. The road through Dent village and up to Dent Station (England's highest mainline railway station) is quiet and atmospheric.
  • Littondale: One of the quietest and most beautiful dales. The road from Arncliffe to Litton is narrow, peaceful, and surrounded by limestone scenery.

Day Ride: Dales Circuit (130 miles)

Skipton → Bolton Abbey → Grassington → Kettlewell → Fleet Moss → Hawes → Buttertubs Pass → Muker → Tan Hill Inn → Brough → Kirkby Stephen → Sedbergh → Ribblehead → Settle → Skipton

The Tan Hill Inn at 1,732ft is England's highest pub. It's worth the detour for the atmosphere, the views, and the bragging rights. The road from Keld to Tan Hill crosses wild, exposed moorland.

Best Times to Visit

  • May-June: Wildflower meadows are at their peak. The Dales are famous for hay meadows full of buttercups, clover, and orchids.
  • September-October: Autumn colours in the valley woodlands, fewer visitors, and clear, crisp riding conditions.
  • Winter: Dramatic but challenging. The high passes may be snow-covered but the low valleys are atmospheric in frost and snow.

Accommodation and Food

The Yorkshire Dales are ideally suited to long weekend motorcycle touring. Base yourself in Hawes — centrally located with excellent facilities including the famous Wensleydale Creamery — or in Settle at the southern end of the park, which has railway connections and good accommodation. The national park has excellent visitor centres at Malham, Hawes, and Reeth providing maps, detailed weather information, and invaluable local knowledge about road conditions and riding highlights.

For food, the Moorcock Inn at the junction of the B6259 and A684 has been serving travellers since the coaching era and remains a welcoming stop for motorcycle tourers. The Green Dragon Inn at Hardraw serves good food and gives access to Hardraw Force waterfall through the pub garden — a unique combination of dining and natural spectacle. Fuel is available in Hawes, Settle, Kirkby Stephen, Richmond, and Skipton — plan your route to pass through these towns for reliable refuelling.

Fleet Moss is the highest road in the Dales at 589m, steep at 1 in 4 in places with a rough surface.
The B6255 through Ribblesdale passes the Ribblehead Viaduct; time your visit to see a train crossing the arches.

faq.q: What is the highest road in the Dales?
faq.a: Fleet Moss is the highest road in the Yorkshire Dales at 589m, connecting Hawes to Buckden. The gradient is steep, reaching 1 in 4 in places, and the surface can be rough, so take it steadily. The exposed moorland setting is dramatic. Buttertubs Pass between Hawes and Thwaite is another classic high road, named for the deep limestone potholes beside it.

faq.q: How do I time a visit to Ribblehead Viaduct?
faq.a: The B6255 from Settle to Hawes passes the Ribblehead Viaduct, one of England's great engineering landmarks on the Settle-Carlisle line. Time your visit to see a train crossing the 24 arches, which makes for a spectacular photograph. Check the Settle-Carlisle timetable in advance. The viaduct is impressive at any time, but a passing train adds scale and drama to the scene.

faq.q: What is a good day ride in the Dales?
faq.a: A satisfying 130-mile circuit starts at Skipton and runs via Bolton Abbey, Grassington, Kettlewell, Fleet Moss, Hawes, Buttertubs Pass, Muker, the Tan Hill Inn, Brough, Kirkby Stephen, Sedbergh, Ribblehead and Settle back to Skipton. This links limestone valleys, high moorland passes and iconic landmarks in a full day, with the Tan Hill Inn a worthwhile detour for the bragging rights.

faq.q: When are the Dales at their best?
faq.a: May and June are superb, when the famous hay meadows are at their peak, full of buttercups, clover and orchids. September and October bring autumn colours to the valley woodlands, fewer visitors and clear, crisp riding conditions. Winter is dramatic but challenging, with high passes such as Fleet Moss potentially snow-covered, though the low valleys are atmospheric in frost and snow.
